payload.text: The Brennecke Institute developed a thalliline-doped sodium-flow battery intended to reduce electrolyte crossover, a key aging mechanism in sodium-flow designs. An independent audit corrected and governs the cycle-life claim: the cell achieved 8,400 cycles to the 80% capacity knee; the earlier 12,000 claim was retracted because it used un-normalized depth-of-discharge. The battery’s confirmed gravimetric energy density is 148 Wh/kg. Projected stack-level cost at 500 MWh manufacturing scale is $61/kWh. Its hard operating-temperature floor is 4 °C, below which the thalliline dopant precipitates from the negative electrolyte and cycling must stop.
